paragraphs: Inside the Venus Hotel, Zhao An leisurely appeared in the corridor. His female bodyguard, who had initially intended to follow him, was left weak and resting in the RV after being sexually assaulted by Zhao An.

Pushing open the door, he found the room already set with food. A hot pot was in the center, and sliced beef and lobster were laid out on the table, even including a special caviar. However, Zhao An wasn't interested in these exotic dishes. Caviar was simply fish roe, nothing special. He hadn't yet grasped the decadent tastes of the wealthy, much like French foie gras—mediocre, even somewhat unpalatable, and ridiculously expensive—a complete rip-off!

"Hey, you look pretty good. Enough with the chit-chat, I'm going to make new energy vehicles. Your brother's already partnered with a foreign company. New energy vehicles are definitely a lucrative market; whoever gets in first will have a head start." Zhao An picked up a slice of beef and dipped it in the hot pot. "You didn't spit in there, did you?"
Huang Meng chuckled, annoyed. "Heh, I'm not that bored."

Even if Huang Meng hadn't said it, Zhao An knew he hadn't. He quickly swished the beef in the hot pot and ate it. "Balance bikes are just a small test. Electric scooters have a wide market, but maintaining them requires some technology. Electric cars have a bright future, and you probably already know why."

Huang Meng quickly realized, "You mean the license plate lottery, right? New energy vehicles don't need a lottery, and even traditional cars are becoming harder to get license plates for now. But how confident are you in making a new energy vehicle? If you can, I'll handle the market."

New energy vehicles are non-fuel vehicles, generally considered to be electric vehicles. Fuel is a non-renewable resource that will eventually run out, and its price is subject to manipulation. Furthermore, current technology is pushing it to the forefront of environmental protection efforts.

Energy-powered vehicles receive subsidies and don't require a license plate lottery. Sustainable vehicles represent the future, but achieving this is difficult. Firstly, the long-distance range of electric vehicles is a problem. The reason gasoline-powered cars are the majority choice is because gas stations are ubiquitous and refueling is convenient. Electric vehicles require unique charging stations, and charging takes a long time, making them inconvenient for travel.

Secondly, the stability of energy-powered vehicles hasn't been resolved. Excessive current can cause spontaneous combustion, even during charging. The underlying technical challenges are extremely difficult to overcome. This initial foray is risky, but once successful, the potential profits are enormous.

The fact that such a real economy sector can receive policy subsidies is already a huge advantage, offering preferential treatment in various aspects. However, technical difficulties have prevented the emergence of energy-powered vehicles in mainland China; they remain largely a gimmick, with most vehicles still being gasoline-powered.
Both Zhao An and Huang Meng are large-scale businessmen. Once you get to one point, the rest is pretty much understood and doesn't require much explanation.

"It's just a consideration; I haven't started preparing yet. There are many ways to open up the market, but why be a pioneer? Heh, the first to try something new certainly makes a lot of money, but the risks are also considerable," Zhao An said with a sinister smile, seemingly intentionally giving a wake-up call.
Huang Meng's pupils widened instantly, as if he had thought of something terrifying. "Are you deliberately trying to get me to promote the leukemia drug?"

"You're not too stupid. Yes, you guessed right, but there's no reward." Zhao An ate large mouthfuls of beef and meatballs, disdainfully ignoring things like lobster and caviar. "Order fifty chicken leg burgers."

A hint of displeasure flashed through Huang Meng's mind. Was this an order? And fifty burgers cost less than a fraction of the price of caviar! He picked up his phone and said, "Order a hundred chicken leg burgers."

"Keep promoting it. Eventually, we'll crush them. Leukemia drugs don't actually make much money; a few hundred million a month isn't high profit." Zhao An was still humble. Making money was fine, but there was no need to be ruthless.
"You think my method is inhumane?" Huang Meng understood what he meant; it was a last resort.

"Keep it up. If you want to beat Huang Yu, you need some capital. Focus on developing the leukemia drug, and then turn the tables on them." Zhao An already had a way to control Bode Pharmaceuticals; these foreign companies were the easiest to deal with. Right now, he was just letting them advertise for him. When the hype was at its peak, he would strike with a better drug and drive them out of the market.

Good money drives out bad—that's a natural market rule. This wasn't Zhao An being despicable; it was simply the law of the jungle. You can't criticize what you've already beaten? Are you going to try to reform them with love? Don't be silly, it's unnecessary and a waste of time and emotion.
"You're really despicable." Huang Meng wiped his cold sweat with a towel. He only now realized that his opponent was such a cunning fellow. "You've already researched the drugs, haven't you?"

"Heh, actually not. Anyway, I can win. You guys can keep jumping around." Zhao An didn't care about such things. He wasn't short of money; he could hold off on betting until the market situation became clear, then strike hard and take over the market in one fell swoop, rather than fish in troubled waters.
At this moment, the waiter pushed in a food cart, placed the prepared hamburgers on the table, mechanically placing the items without saying a word.

Wait until you can withstand your older brother's advances before we talk. Also, figure out a way to get out of here soon. If things get out of hand, you won't be able to handle it." Liao Ruomin's hands and feet were indeed cold.

Even if the mother and daughter spent together, thirty million would be a stretch.
Thinking this way, Zhao An's refusal to help seemed to be a valid reason.
Liao Ruomin's thoughts were becoming increasingly erratic, and she was starting to lose her senses.
Her head was spinning from the barrage of news; she was finding it difficult to make rational judgments.
She needed to calm down and think carefully about what to do!
Qin Xue sighed, "Your sister and I became Zhao An's mistresses together to pay off our debts.
We had no other choice.
I hope you can understand; after all, thirty million is no small sum.

To win over such a woman, one either had to rape her or outsmart her. Although rape wouldn't be a big deal—she could still be made to feel good—Zhao An wouldn't do that. He wanted to make Liao Ruomin fall into his trap, obediently bow her head to him, and beg him in the most humble tone. He wanted her to swallow all her pride and arrogance.

Qin Xue actually had no feelings for her ex-husband anymore, and hadn't even visited him. Everything was an act to please her man, Zhao An. She was willing to give up everything, even her daughter and her mother. Her shameless pregnancy with Zhao An's child shows she had fallen; not only had her heart fallen for him, but even her vagina had taken the shape of his penis. She was a wife who had been sexually assaulted countless times, and after being violated countless times, she had fallen in love with the boy who had forced her.
Hearing her mother's words, Liao Ruomin felt a pang of sorrow and bitterness in her heart. She hugged her mother tightly, "Mom, you've worked so hard."

"It's not hard at all. As long as you can both find jobs smoothly, that's all that matters. I don't have much ability right now, and I hope you won't be influenced by me and change yourself. There's no turning back now. I've fallen in love with your sister's classmate, and I'm pregnant with his child. I just want to tell you the whole truth so you can make the best judgment yourself. Qin Xue patted her eldest daughter's hand. "Mom knows, you can put it away now. That's enough, I'm going back now." She then got up and left.
"Mom, let me see you off." Liao Ruomin was about to say something when the door opened again, and there came her younger sister, Liao Ruoxia.

Her clothes had an inexplicable sense of style; although she didn't know how much they cost, they certainly weren't cheap. What had happened to her sister?
"Xia! How could this happen!" Liao Ruomin covered her mouth, unable to believe that her sister had changed so much.

"Mom, you go back to the car and wait. I'll talk to my sister." Liao Ruoxia casually took out a cigarette and lit it. Her practiced movements gave her a slightly rebellious, almost delinquent air, like a troubled teenager about to do something.

Qin Xue nodded, then walked away in her high heels, clutching her aching back. Pregnancy seemed to be a significant burden for her. If Zhao An saw her, he'd definitely be overcome with lust. Nothing was more alluring than seeing a still-attractive, charming mature woman clutching her aching back. Such a seductive pose—it would be a shame not to have sex with her.

She deeply hated men because of a boyfriend she had in college who cheated on her with her best friend. This disgusted her, and that's why she hated men so much.

Liao Ruoxia retorted, each word like a hammer blow to Liao Ruomin's heart. This soul-searching question was driving her to the brink of collapse. How could she possibly play this game?

paragraphs: In the city hospital ward, a leukemia patient had recovered and was under observation, undergoing a full-body check-up and monitoring. This treatment was free; everything was free. However, the price was confidentiality. Any leak would result in a minimum of ten million yuan in damages according to the contract, and would also be recorded in the credit system. As for the consequences of a lost credit record, that was another matter entirely.

Bai Qiuqin observed for a moment, her eyes narrowed. The medication was quite effective; at least the patient had recovered from the disease's symptoms. Now in a stable phase, it all seemed so unbelievable.

The treatment for leukemia aimed to kill the diseased cells while restoring the body's hematopoietic function. Only when blood circulated could the body's organs and tissues receive nutrition. It sounded simple, but in practice, it was incredibly difficult, almost impossible. It was like going to the moon; the moon was in the sky, and how to get there was simply to fly upwards.

Listen, how simple—just fly upwards. Normal people think like this, completely oblivious to the factors involved and what needs to be considered. Flying too high can lead to oxygen deprivation, a sudden drop in temperature, and the influence of wind—these are all things that need to be taken into account.

After seeing the patient's condition report, Bai Qiuqin breathed a sigh of relief, her heart filled with complex emotions. She couldn't believe that a man who spent all his time with women could be so successful. It was utterly unbelievable, and she couldn't understand where he would find the time to conduct experiments. How could he invent something without experimentation?

The British have already spent over 20 billion dollars on research into a treatment for chronic leukemia, and that was only in its early stages, taking over twenty years. The cost was enormous, and it was the result of countless people working together.
And Zhao An? She hadn't seen him have any time for experiments at all. How could someone like that inexplicably invent a drug for leukemia?

Bai Qiuqin was a very rational woman, knowing how to overcome her weaknesses and suppress her curiosity. But this time, she couldn't suppress it. Zhao An was too outstanding. This man was like a firefly in the dark night; she couldn't help but notice him—he was too dazzling.
"Zhao An, you truly amaze me. Let me see what other secrets you have!" Bai Qiuqin said, picking up the phone and dialing her secretary. "Where is Zhao An now?"
Zhao An had just been here, but he only glanced at the report and left without even looking at it. Just a glance, truly a glance, as if he didn't have time to look any longer.
The secretary answered truthfully, "He said he wasn't feeling well and went to a VIP ward to have a doctor and nurse examine him."

"Not feeling well? Having a doctor? What happened to him?" Bai Qiuqin was puzzled. What was going on? Was he really sick? She had no idea that Zhao An always called female doctors, and the nurses, of course, were all women.
"It's not clear yet. I haven't gone to see him," the secretary replied.

"Okay, I understand." Bai Qiuqin hung up the phone, her eyes narrowed. She sensed something was wrong; there seemed to be a problem. Thinking this, she stood up, grabbed her handbag and phone, and left the office, instructing everyone to ensure the confidentiality and security of the premises before departing.

Shortly afterward, Bai Qiuqin arrived at the VIP ward. No one was allowed to enter, but she was different; she had access privileges. As she approached ward number five, she heard giggling and some strange noises. This piqued her curiosity even more. She couldn't help but lean closer, cautiously peering inside.
She saw Zhao An lying on the hospital bed, still dressed in a patient's gown. His expression was incredibly lewd. "Doctor, I'm in so much pain here! Please check me; I can't breathe!"

Her white coat barely reached her upper thighs, revealing a pair of long, slender legs in flesh-colored stockings, her fair skin almost overflowing from the fabric. She wore ten-centimeter strappy high heels, the straps looping around the corners, exposing most of her delicate, white feet, making her appear exceptionally sexy and alluring.
